ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated Sanctions List, Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2020, and the Cayman Islands Counter-Money Laundering/Counter-Financing of Terrorism sanctions screening obligations. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) require enhanced due diligence with annual refresh and source-of-wealth verification. Independent screening must include World-Check/Refinitiv and negative-news databases, block-chain analytics for USDC-linked transactions, and continuous transaction monitoring, given the medium-risk nature of the commercial scraping and proxy API business.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cayman Islands General Registry - Companies Online Registration System (CORE); Gibraltar Companies Registry - eRegistry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Both jurisdictions require company names to be submitted in Romanized English characters; English is the sole official legal language. Cayman law requires the proposed name to be distinguishable from existing registered names and not deemed undesirable. Gibraltar law requires an overseas company name to be distinguishable from names already on the Gibraltar register; if the name is unacceptable, the Registrar may direct the registrant to adopt an alternative name for Gibraltar purposes. No transliteration into a local script is required.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 business days of rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the relevant Registrar, attaching the original rejection notice, a statutory declaration explaining the grounds for contesting the refusal, a list of alternative names, and supporting trademark consent letters where applicable. The Registrar must issue a determination within 10 business days. If the appeal is unsuccessful, a fresh name application may be submitted after 6 months. The final administrative remedy is an application for judicial review before the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands or the Supreme Court of Gibraltar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the statutory registered office for the Cayman Exempted Company; a physical, licensed registered office in the Cayman Islands is mandatory. A virtual office in Gibraltar may be used for administrative correspondence, but only if a licensed Gibraltar corporate services provider maintains a physical authorized agent address for service of process. For this ISIC 6201 data-pipeline and API business, banks and EMIs may require additional substance indicators, including local director residency, board meeting minutes, and commercial contracts, before accepting a virtual-office arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-low risk. Unannounced on-site inspections by the Cayman Islands Registrar or Cayman Islands Monetary Authority are rare but possible in routine AML/CFT supervision. The Gibraltar Financial Services Commission may conduct desk-based or on-site inspections under the AML/CFT framework, with a 20% likelihood within the first 12 months given the cross-border, medium-risk commercial profile and cryptocurrency payment rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2023 Revision), as amended, especially sections 5, 7, 8, 9, 14, 20, 34 and 38; for a Gibraltar commercial access point, also Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (overseas company registration provisions) and Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar) regarding non-resident tax-exempt status.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands General Registry; Gibraltar Companies House as secondary registry for any overseas company/branch registration in Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Cayman: Application for Reservation and/or Registration (Form CR1) together with the approved Memorandum and Articles of Association. Gibraltar branch (if established): prescribed overseas company registration form published by Gibraltar Companies House, filed with certified copy of the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Cayman Exempted Company; one or more shares may be issued, typically one ordinary share of USD 1 fully subscribed and paid on allotment. No capital duty, escrow account, or paid-in capital verification is required under Cayman law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Certificate of Incorporation dated [●] is noted and the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act (2023 Revision) is ratified. That the subscription of 1 ordinary share at USD 1 by the subscriber is approved and allotted in accordance with the Memorandum and Articles. That the registered office at [registered office address, Grand Cayman] is adopted as the Company’s official registered office. That [●] is appointed sole director and [●] is appointed corporate secretary, each to serve until otherwise resolved. That the directors and registered agent are authorised to make statutory filings, open bank or EMI accounts, and execute all incidental documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry eServices portal (online name reservation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name and, if appropriate, one alternate name through the Cayman General Registry eServices portal. Pay the name reservation fee and await Registry approval. The registered agent must simultaneously complete AML/KYC verification of the subscriber and ultimate beneficial owner, including source-of-funds confirmation, before incorporation proceeds.
required_dossiers: Certified passport and proof of residential address of each subscriber/UBO
Registered agent engagement letter and AML/KYC questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or objected to, file a revised name within 5 working days. Any KYC documentation query should be answered within 10 days with supplemental evidence of source of funds or beneficial ownership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman registered agent or notary public under the Cayman Islands Companies Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association with one subscriber. The subscriber must sign before the registered agent or a notary public, and the signatures must be witnessed as required. The Articles may authorise a single director, flexible share capital, and an exempted-company scope restricted to offshore activities. Prepare English translation if any constitutional document is bilingual.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective execution or missing witness signatures are cured by re-signature or by a corrective amendment filed within 7 days. If the Articles conflict with the Companies Act, file a written consent to amend before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Statutory Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands General Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application with the Registrar, including the signed Memorandum and Articles, the statutory declaration of compliance by the registered agent, the prescribed application form, and payment of the government incorporation fee. Provide the registered office and registered agent details in the application. The Registrar may issue queries on AML documentation before approving incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A Registry query is answered within 14 days by the registered agent with corrected forms and supplemental documents. A refused application can be resubmitted after correction; priority of the original filing is retained where the Registrar confirms no substantive defect.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office of HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax), Portland House, Glacis Road, Gibraltar GX11 1AA; official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation. Company registration: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar. Customs: HM Customs Gibraltar. Data protection: Gibraltar Regulatory Authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: If the Cayman Exempted Company establishes a physical place of business in Gibraltar, it must register as an 'external company' with the Registrar of Companies within 30 days, filing certified copies of the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, register of directors and secretary, and a Gibraltar registered address and process agent. Step 2: The Income Tax Office then issues a Gibraltar company reference number (TIN), either automatically on companies-registry data exchange or on filing Form IT-R1 under the Income Tax Act; this TIN governs corporation tax, PAYE, and all fiscal filings. Step 3: If carrying on a qualifying activity (data/API services qualify), the company must File a Genuine Link / economic substance return evidencing local premises, Gibraltar-resident directors, and board meetings held in Gibraltar. Step 4: Register as a data controller with the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority under the Data Protection Act (GDPR-incorporated) because the business involves scraping and processing web data. Step 5: No Gibraltar VAT registration exists; separately assess UK VAT registration if UK private-consumer digital services exceed GBP 85,000 in any rolling 12 months, and verify EU member-state or non-Union OSS obligations for EU consumer sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the Cayman Exempted Company holds a 30-year Cayman Tax Exemption Certificate (Tax Concessions Act) and is tax-exempt in the Cayman Islands; in Gibraltar it is treated as a non-resident company where central management and control is exercised outside Gibraltar. Only Gibraltar-source income is taxable at the 10% corporate rate; no capital gains tax, no net-worth tax, no withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties, and no branch remittance tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar provides no US-style 'check-the-box' election. Relevant mechanisms: (1) transition from Gross Income Based Tax (GIBT) to standard chargeable-profits assessment — GIBT is being phased out and the standard 10% corporation tax on chargeable profits applies from financial year 2025; (2) non-resident companies require no election — automatic taxation on Gibraltar-source income only; (3) hybrid mismatch designations under the Income Tax (Hybrid Mismatch) Regulations for structured UK/EU financing and IP arrangements; (4) optional UK VAT registration under the non-UK-established business rules where UK B2C digital-services turnover is below the mandatory threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT or GST — Gibraltar applies no general value-added, goods-and-services, or sales tax. Indirect levies are limited to import duty, purchase tax on a closed list of goods (alcohol, tobacco, fuel, luxury vehicles), and stamp duty. Cross-border digital services (web-scraping API subscriptions, proxy-gateway usage fees) are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect taxation; UK VAT may apply where private consumers resident in the UK are supplied.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A in Gibraltar pounds (GIP) — there is no VAT, therefore no turnover threshold for indirect-tax registration. Mandatory triggers are: (i) external-company registration with Companies House Gibraltar within 30 days of establishing a Gibraltar place of business (no turnover threshold); (ii) HM Customs registration for importers, arising at first importation with no de-minimis turnover limit; (iii) UK VAT registration once UK-resident private-consumer digital-service sales exceed GBP 85,000 in any rolling 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted below that threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time e-invoicing, continuous transaction control (CTC), fiscal clearance, or digital stamping mandate exists in Gibraltar. Invoices must contain standard commercial particulars (supplier and customer identity, description, consideration, date) but require no government clearance or cryptographic stamp. Customs declarations are submitted electronically via HM Customs Gibraltar's single administrative entry system. UK Making Tax Digital (MTD) requirements are irrelevant unless the company registers for UK VAT, in which case MTD-compatible digital record-keeping applies only to UK VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — Gibraltar imposes no VAT, so there is no export zero-rating or refund mechanism to claim. Exports of services, including web-scraping API access and proxy-gateway subscriptions, are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax regardless of customer location; no output tax arises and no input tax is recoverable. For UK VAT purposes, if the company registers, cross-border B2B supplies remain outside the scope of UK VAT under place-of-supply rules, and UK zero-rating applies only to physically exported goods, not to these intangible services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs electronic import/export declaration (customs entry) where any physical goods or media move through Gibraltar
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Certificate of Origin (UK-Gibraltar Trade Agreement evidence or EUR1/ATR where preferential tariff treatment is claimed)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 records evidencing customer settlement, required by the Income Tax Office to substantiate the non-resident or Gibraltar-source income return
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No Gibraltar VAT export clawback exists. Scrutiny instead targets income characterisation, substance, and cross-border compliance: (i) incorrect Income Tax returns attract default interest up to 8% per annum and penalties up to 100% of the tax undercharged; (ii) false customs declarations result in forfeiture of goods and fines up to three times the duty evaded; (iii) failure to satisfy the Genuine Link economic-substance return can trigger residence recharacterisation, information exchange with the Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority, and retrospective assessment at 10% on worldwide income; (iv) UK HMRC may assess and penalise undeclared UK VAT registration (up to 100% of the VAT due plus daily penalties) if the GBP 85,000 threshold is crossed; (v) USDC or other cryptocurrency settlement does not alter the tax position and must be supported by invoices and blockchain records evidencing consideration and customer identity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Currency) issues the Gibraltar pound (GIP), pegged at 1:1 to GBP; prudential regulation and AML/CTF supervision are executed by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC). The Bank of England constitutes the de facto monetary anchor through the GIP/GBP parity, and HM Treasury retains ultimate sovereign authority over the British Overseas Territory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account. No exchange-control statute restricts capital injections, profit repatriation, dividend distributions, or cross-border service-fee receipts in Gibraltar. The Cayman exempted company may remit profits to shareholders through Gibraltar correspondent banking without prior regulatory approval, subject only to bank-level source-of-funds documentary verification. No Gibraltar withholding tax applies to outbound dividends or interest, easing the profit-remittance path; the tax-exempt Cayman status of the entity itself does not obstruct conversion but elevates the documentary burden at bank onboarding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Gibraltar maintains a zero-surrender regime: no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to repatriate foreign-currency export or service-export proceeds. USD and EUR receipts may be retained in original currency, converted to GIP/GBP at market rate, or routed onward for trade settlement at the company's discretion without central-bank registration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (GBP/EUR/USD); segregated capital escrow account available pre-trade
Operational account with multi-currency clearing and short-term treasury deposits
Operational account with documented appetite for fintech and digital-asset-linked corporate clients
Private corporate account with treasury/hedging desk and cross-border wealth management

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-Medium. Major UK/Gibraltar fintech EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, and Gibraltar-licensed electronic-money platforms) generally classify Cayman Exempted Companies as non-EEA offshore high-risk structures and reject onboarding absent a pre-existing prime-bank relationship and Gibraltar-fiduciary introduction. EU e-money institutions frequently embargo Cayman Islands incorporations outright, particularly where the commercial activity comprises web-scraping APIs. Viable alternatives: (1) a Gibraltar-licensed EMI route conditioned on enhanced due diligence, a registered Gibraltar agent, and a full source-of-funds pack; (2) USDC stablecoin treasury rails executed through regulated custodians (Coinbase Prime or Circle account) for Stripe-paired merchant settlements and supplier payouts. No Gibraltar statute prohibits EMI onboarding of a Cayman vehicle, but each EMI's risk appetite is proprietary and a legal opinion plus verifiable operational substance is effectively mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate exists for physical board presence in Gibraltar; remote corporate onboarding of a Cayman exempted company is permitted where signatories complete video e-KYC and a licensed fiduciary makes the introduction. In practice tier-1 banks require: (1) a live video interview with the ultimate beneficial owner and each account signatory; (2) certified passport and secondary-ID; (3) a notarised board resolution authorising account opening; and (4) a board-registered address in Gibraltar where the bank demands a local service address. Private banks such as SG Hambros may still require an in-person UBO meeting at the Gibraltar branch or a group office abroad, which is achievable through the Cayman director's home jurisdiction if a group office exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman Islands Exempted Company automated risk flag as offshore tax-haven jurisdiction; perceived ownership opacity and zero minimum capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Certificate of Good Standing from the Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies; certified Memorandum and Articles of Association; certified register of directors and members; Cayman Economic Substance Notification and self-certification demonstrating either pure-holding status or demonstrable substance for relevant activities; Gibraltar AML/CTF beneficial-ownership declaration filed with the appointed reporting entity; legal opinion from a Gibraltar-licensed law firm confirming beneficial-ownership transparency and the non-sham nature of the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 6201 public web-scraping and proxy API gateway activity flagged for data-privacy sensitivity, reputational risk, and possible regulatory exposure in destination markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GDPR and UK Data Protection Act 2018 (as extended to Gibraltar) compliance policy; product terms of service and data-use disclaimers prohibiting collection or resale of personal data; end-client KYC and onboarding log evidencing vetting of API subscribers; domain whitelist and robots.txt compliance protocol; records of legal-basis assessment for targeted scraping; confirmation from the GFSC Privacy Commissioner's office or ICO that no data-licensing statutory licence applies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual payment rails comprising Stripe fiat settlement and USDC cryptocurrency exposure create financial-crime and sanctions red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CTF policy aligned with the Financial Services Act 2019 and GFSC AML rules; source-of-funds declaration with substantiating bank statements for initial capital; wallet attestation for all USDC treasury addresses; blockchain analytics compliance certificate (Chainalysis or equivalent) demonstrating no sanctioned-entity exposure; USDC conversion policy fixing fiat conversion at treasury entry; sanctions screening records against OFAC/EU/UN lists for all counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated exempted company with no audited financials and no operating history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder letter of comfort or bank reference from an incident bank; management accounts or 12-month pro-forma revenue projection; signed hosting/licensing contracts evidencing active commercial operations; introduction and continuing due-diligence undertaking by a licensed Gibraltar fiduciary under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015; confirmation that all economic activity generating bank turnover will flow through the Gibraltar account enabling transaction monitoring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from members must be routed via SWIFT wire from the shareholder's home jurisdiction into the Gibraltar operational or escrow account denominated in GBP, EUR, or USD. Gibraltar imposes no statutory purpose-code statistical regime; the MT103 narrative must state 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION – SHARE CAPITAL – EXEMPTED CO' and be matched against: (1) the board resolution authorising share issuance, (2) the Cayman share register entry, and (3) the certified MT103 copy. Sale proceeds arriving via Stripe settle through Stripe's banking partners in the settlement currency and require the corresponding Stripe payout report and monthly reconciliation as audit evidence. USDC injections execute over Ethereum or Polygon from a previously whitelisted wallet, with the amount converted at the mid-market reference rate recorded at treasury entry and the transaction hash archived.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 is the sole fiat clearing rail for trade settlements, including cloud-hosting, data-centre, licencing, and engineering out-payments. Commercial letters of credit are impractical for the API-services trade model and are disrecommended. Supplier and vendor payments should be batched with each MT103 referencing the underlying invoice and the vendor's tax-identification number. USDC-denominated disbursements settle on Polygon or Ethereum exclusively to whitelisted licensed-exchange custodians and vetted suppliers, subject to mandatory dual-approval sign-off, invoice-to-hash matching, daily USD-nominal reconciliation, and a 24-hour finality buffer before executing the blockchain transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards: GIP/USD and GBP/USD forwards up to 12 months are permissible with authorised Gibraltar banks to fix the conversion of USD-denominated Stripe revenue into GBP operating currency.

Non-deliverable forwards: Not applicable to GIP because of full convertibility and GBP parity; OTC GBP/USD NDFs via the London market are acceptable only for offshore investors holding the non-GBP leg and require a bank-approved ISDA master agreement.

Cross-currency swaps: GBP/USD cross-currency interest-rate swaps on notional treasury balances are permissible under a signed ISDA/CSA where the purpose is to match the duration of receivables and payables, not speculative profit-taking.

FX options and zero-cost collars: Vanilla GBP/USD put and call options with payable premium, or a zero-cost collar, are accessible through the SG Hambros treasury desk and admissible for hedging forecast annual revenue within a board-approved treasury policy that expressly prohibits speculative trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Annual Return (Form B) and annual registration fee under Section 61, Cayman Companies Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA - Companies Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation; no extension. Standard fee tier assumes authorized share capital up to KYD 50,000; higher tier applies above that threshold.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic KYD 500 late-filing penalty plus daily default surcharges; sustained non-payment triggers Gazette strike-off notice under Section 146 with dissolution and asset forfeiture to the Crown; directors remain liable for continuing default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Return (ESR) with foreign tax-residency declaration (tax-resident in Gibraltar; Cayman substance test disapplied)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Information Authority / CIMA International Tax Co-operation Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of each financial period, aligned to the Gibraltar accounting year (e.g., 31 December following a calendar year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Level 1 penalty up to KYD 10,000; Level 2 up to KYD 100,000; Level 3 daily penalties for continuing non-compliance; the Tax Information Authority may recommend strike-off. Gibraltar Tax Identification Number and tax-residence certificate must accompany the declaration.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (Gibraltar standard CIT rate); 0% Cayman statutory rate for the Exempted Company.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cayman Tax Exemption Certificate provides 30-year nil Cayman tax; Gibraltar small-profits rate 10% on first GBP 425,000; Gibraltar Patent Box 50% deduction on qualifying IP income (effective 6.25%); no capital gains tax in Cayman or Gibraltar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Company Tax Return (Form CIT1) filed via the HM Government of Gibraltar Income Tax Office e-Portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; one CIT1 return for each chargeable accounting period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Not later than 12 months after the end of the chargeable accounting period; for a 31 December year-end, due 31 December of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, Gibraltar tax reference, registered office, country of incorporation, and location of central management and control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 'Cayman Exempted Company'; identify the Cayman registered office and disclose whether board meetings and commercial decisions are taken in Gibraltar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable accounting period start and end dates (ISO 8601 format).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the accounting period of the Gibraltar branch/PE; non-residents file for periods that are not treated as a Gibraltar resident assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net chargeable profits before deductions, including worldwide API gateway and web-scraping subscription receipts if Gibraltar-resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only Gibraltar-source trading profits attributable to the PE; do not include non-Gibraltar foreign income unless arising from a Gibraltar PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and capital allowances, including the 50% patent-box deduction for qualifying software IP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses and capital allowances directly attributable to the Gibraltar PE; attach contemporaneous TP documentation for intragroup service fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after deductions and reliefs (Box 3 less Box 4).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the PE's separately computed taxable profit; do not offset foreign losses against PE profit unless a treaty permits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax liability at the 10% lower rate on the first GBP 425,000 and 12.5% on the excess; subtract foreign tax credits and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same rate bands to PE profits; non-residents may not take Cayman tax credits because Cayman imposes no tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: incremental fixed penalties of GBP 100, GBP 300 and GBP 1,000 at 3, 6 and 12 months; daily GBP 60 surcharge after 12 months; tax-geared penalty up to 100% of tax at risk; interest at 8% per annum; criminal liability for fraudulent evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (no Gibraltar or Cayman dividend withholding tax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Although domestic withholding is nil, a payor seeking formal treaty protection should (i) obtain a Gibraltar Tax Residence Certificate from the ITO, (ii) obtain a Cayman Tax Exemption Certificate evidencing Cayman tax residence status, (iii) file Form CIT-DTA with the Gibraltar ITO, and (iv) attach a beneficial ownership declaration and the relevant DTA Article analysis before the dividend distribution; the UK-Gibraltar arrangement and Cayman's bilateral information exchange framework are the relevant instruments.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory rate for royalties and interest in both Gibraltar and Cayman; under the UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement, royalty and interest payments to UK residents generally remain free of Gibraltar withholding if the recipient has no Gibraltar PE.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GBP 1,000,000 aggregate controlled transactions requiring a Gibraltar Local File; Master File required when group consolidated global turnover exceeds GBP 50,000,000; Cayman Economic Substance Return required for every relevant activity irrespective of thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cayman ESR applies to the API distribution and IP holding functions; a Cayman tax-resident company must maintain Cayman office, full-time staff, and local operating expenditure, or, if claiming Gibraltar tax residence, file the Cayman economic substance return with a Gibraltar TRC and demonstrate board meetings, staff, and decision-making in Gibraltar. Gibraltar applies economic substance/substance-over-form to the small-profits rate and patent box; artificial arrangements with no real revenue-producing activity will be disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting Stripe and USDC subscription revenue from CIT1 Box 3, or routing invoices through a dormant Cayman shell while control and employees are in Gibraltar, to make taxable profit nil.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty up to 100% of the underpaid tax, plus interest at 8% per annum; criminal conviction carries an unlimited fine and imprisonment for up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who know of or cause the false return are jointly and severally liable for penalties; courts may pierce the corporate veil, impose travel bans, freeze assets, and issue extradition requests through the UK-Gibraltar criminal assistance framework.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording all API gateway revenue in the Cayman entity while paying the Gibraltar operating entity a non-arm's-length 1% commission, leaving no taxable profit despite substantial Gibraltar-based staff, servers, and customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gibraltar transfer-pricing adjustment increases taxable profit to arm's-length; additional 12.5% CIT, compound interest at 8%, and tax-geared penalties up to 100% of the adjustment; secondary adjustment may deem a dividend or loan to the Cayman parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving undocumented or unrealistically priced intercompany transactions are personally liable for penalties and disgorgement; in egregious cases, the court lifts the corporate veil and applies director disqualification orders and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Cayman Exempted Company holds IP and bank accounts, has no office or staff in Cayman, and also fails to evidence Gibraltar tax residence, becoming a stateless shell that pays no tax anywhere.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cayman ESR fines: initial CI$12,000, then CI$12,000 per month, up to CI$120,000; on indictment, fine up to CI$120,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for false declarations; Gibraltar may impute tax residency and levy 12.5% CIT on all worldwide profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false economic substance returns are personally liable; Cayman courts may impose travel bans, asset freezes, and director disqualification; UK authorities can use the 'offshore entity' provisions to recover taxes from controlling persons.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing merchant API subscriptions via Stripe and USDC without sufficient AML/KYC controls, failing to register as a payment services provider, or accepting crypto from sanctioned jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission penalties up to GBP 1,000,000 per breach or 5% of annual turnover; criminal fines for sanctions/anti-terrorism lapses are unlimited with imprisonment up to 7 years; Stripe/merchant accounts may be suspended and funds confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior managers and directors face personal criminal liability for failures to submit SARs and for AML programme deficiencies; travel bans, confiscation orders, and extradition to UK courts can be imposed.
